title: Buffets, Carveries & Hot-Holding
blurb: Keeping buffet and carvery food safe: hot and cold temperatures, contamination, topping up and allergens.
siteNotes: Where the probe thermometers are kept and where buffet temperature records are written
Which sneeze screens, serving utensils and labels the venue uses for wedding and event buffets
legalNotes: Hot food held at 63°C or above and cold food at 8°C or below are the figures in the trainer and match the usual food temperature control rules for England; the trainer gives no time limit for food that falls out of temperature, so none is stated here.
Allergen labelling and information on buffets: see the allergens session; the trainer says only that dishes should be clearly labelled.

cards.title: Buffets, Carveries & Hot-Holding
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- keep hot and cold food at the right temperatures
- protect displayed food from contamination
- swap dishes instead of topping them up

cards.title: Why buffets are risky
cards.body:
Weddings and events often mean buffets and carveries, where food sits out on display for a while. That is exactly where food safety can slip.

There are two enemies.

items.title: The danger zone
items.text: Food at the wrong temperature for too long

cards.title: Hot stays hot, cold stays cold
cards.body:
Hot food on display must be kept hot. Cold food must be kept cold.

Check and record the temperatures regularly through the service. Food that falls out of safe temperature can only be left out for a limited time before it must be used or thrown away, so watch the clock as well as the thermometer.

cards.title: Protect the food
cards.body: Guests should never be using their hands to serve themselves.

left.title: Do
items: Give each dish its own serving utensil

cards.title: Swap it, never top it up
cards.body:
When a dish runs low, replace it with a fresh, clean container.

Do not top up the old one. Topping up mixes older food with new and lets bacteria build up.

cards.title: Labels and utensils
cards.body: Do not forget allergens on a buffet.

items.title: Utensils stay put
items.text: Keep each utensil with its own dish

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Hot food at 63°C or above, cold food at 8°C or below
- Check and record temperatures regularly, and watch the clock
- Sneeze screens, and a separate utensil for each dish
- Swap a low dish for a fresh container; never top it up
- Label allergens and keep utensils with their own dish

cards.q: Hot food on display must be kept at:
options: Below 40°C
Any temperature if it looks hot
Above 30°C so it stays warm
63°C or above
cards.why: Hot food on display must be kept hot: 63°C or above.

cards.q: Cold food on display should be kept at 8°C or below.
cards.why: Cold food must be kept cold, at 8°C or below.

cards.q: When a buffet dish runs low, what should you do instead of topping it up?
options: Replace it with a fresh, clean container
Stir the new food in to mix it well
Add a little at a time as guests serve
Move it to the warmest spot to refresh it
cards.why: Replace the dish with a fresh, clean container. Topping up mixes older food with new.

cards.q: You should top up the old container to save washing up.
cards.why: Topping up lets bacteria build up. Swap the dish for a fresh, clean container instead.

options: No utensils, so guests use tongs from the table
One shared spoon for the whole buffet
A serving utensil kept with that dish
A spoon that guests pass along the line
cards.why: Each dish has its own serving utensil, so guests are not using their hands and allergens do not transfer.

cards.q: Sneeze screens help protect displayed food from contamination.
cards.why: Sneeze screens and separate utensils protect food from the many guests helping themselves.

cards.q: Why is topping up an old dish with fresh food risky?
options: It makes the portions look too big
It mixes older food with new and lets bacteria build up
It cools the hot food down too fast
It hides the allergen label on the dish
cards.why: Topping up mixes older food with new, and bacteria can build up.

cards.q: Buffet dishes should be clearly labelled for allergens.
cards.why: Do not forget allergens on a buffet: dishes should be clearly labelled.

options: Guessed by eye during service
Checked and recorded regularly
Checked only when a guest complains
Taken once at the start of service
cards.why: Check and record temperatures regularly throughout the service.

cards.q: Keeping utensils with their own dish helps avoid transferring allergens.
cards.why: A utensil moved between dishes carries allergens with it, so each stays with its own dish.
